findings.source: Decode.lean scanLexical escape branch; Encode.lean escapeJsonString/jsonObj; CanonicalJson.lean lexString; probes/escaped-key/attempt2 and extra
findings.issue: Distinct source-map keys a+newline and literal au000a serialize as a\u000a and au000a. lexString decodes \u000a to newline. scanLexical treats a backslash as a one-character skip and appends the following character, so both keys become au000a and it reports duplicateKey au000a. decodeBytes therefore fails. parseCanonicalJson plus decodeDecodedIR succeeds. Observed size 3453, depth 6, max array 32, source-map sorted true. Independent attempt2 stdout hash matches the root diagnostic exactly. True duplicate key same is refused by both scanner and parser. A lone newline key scans as ok under the corrupted identity. Preserving the full canonical string domain requires scanner repair. This is a concrete scanner defect, not a kernel-proved admissible counterexample.

actual.true_duplicate: scanner and parser both duplicateKey same

parseStep_* equalities are context-general definitional facts. parse_arr_feed_elem and parse_obj_field_* assume a successful child foldlM (h_feed / h_val) and then append comma or key/colon. parse_obj_field_step's _h_not_dup is unused. These are compositional step facts. They do not prove recursive inversion of arbitrary nested arrays and objects.

Scalar parser inverses for party/asset/domain/partyRef/cellRef are enumeration case splits. parseCanonicalJson_encodeRat_witness is only RatEnc 0/1. parseCanonicalJson_encodeCell_witness is only the main/alice/usd cell. Generic encoded numeric/rational parser inversion is not proved by those fixed examples.
